headline: STAKEHOLDER GOLD CLOSES 498m LOKI DISCOVERY HOLE FULLY MINERALIZED — Cu-Ni-Co-PGE System Confirmed In Yukon White Gold District; Second Target Defined
snippet: Stakeholder Gold Corp. (TSX-V: SKHRF) has completed final assays for hole BA2601 at the Loki Critical Mineral Zone on its Ballarat Gold-Copper Project in the Yukon White Gold District, confirming copper-nickel-cobalt and platinum-group-element mineralization throughout the full 498-metre discovery hole. The strongest base-metal response returned 3,730 ppm Cu, 641 ppm Ni, and 514 ppm Co at 5.02% sulphur within a 6-metre zone averaging 1,190 ppm Cu. Mineralization occurs as disseminated, blebby and locally net-textured to massive magmatic sulphides — a signature consistent with a fertile magmatic intrusive system. 3D inversion modelling of VTEM and magnetic data over the Loki area has defined a second discrete conductive target to the south, untested by drilling. Magmatic Cu-Ni-Co-PGE systems in established gold districts are exactly the critical minerals intersection that re-rates junior projects in the current policy environment.

headline: GOLIATH SUREBET WEDGE ZONES CONFIRMED: BROAD INTERVALS CONNECT BONANZA AND GOLDEN GATE — 46 Gold Lodes Defined, 7 Rigs, 50,000m Golden Triangle Program
snippet: Goliath Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: GOT) announced August 31 that newly defined volcanic Wedge Zones comprised of gold-bearing quartz-sulphide mineralization — including the VG-NE zone — are confirmed in broad intervals directly between the structural intersection of the Bonanza and Golden Gate zones at the Surebet Discovery in B.C.'s Golden Triangle. Collectively the discovery now encompasses 46 gold-rich lodes/veins and multiple subvertical Eocene-aged dyke swarms, with 100% of holes drilled to date intersecting quartz-sulphide mineralization and 92% returning visible gold. The announcement confirms that the structural corridor connecting Bonanza and Golden Gate is mineralized, not just the zones themselves — a material increase in the potential volume of gold-bearing rock at Surebet. The fully funded 50,000m 2026 program continues with 7 drill rigs across all zones.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD SENDS SPYGLASS TO 330m DEPTH — 9.40 g/t Au Over 4.60m As High-Grade Zone Nearly Doubles Vertically At Gold Rock, Ontario
snippet: Dryden Gold Corp. (TSX-V: DRY) released August 31 deep-drilling results confirming the Spyglass high-grade zone at its Gold Rock project in Ontario has extended from approximately 190 metres to 330 metres true depth. Drill hole DGR-073 assayed 9.40 g/t gold over 4.60 metres including a 78.40 g/t gold over 0.38 metres bonanza. Adjacently, the Buccaneer zone was extended from 185 metres to 370 metres depth — nearly doubling the interpreted Buccaneer footprint. The twin-zone depth extensions at Spyglass and Buccaneer are a structural signal that the Gold Rock system has open continuity well below current resource limits, maintaining potential for a substantial resource upgrade in the ongoing fully funded 45,000m drill program.

headline: ROXMORE CONVERSE NEVADA: 94.5m AT 0.73 g/t AU — PFS Targeted For 2027 As 3-Rig, 30,000m Phase 1 Builds Bulk Resource On Battle Mountain Trend
snippet: Roxmore Resources Inc. (TSX: RM) released September 1 additional infill and extension drill results from the Converse Gold Project on the Battle Mountain–Eureka Trend in Nevada: hole CV26-022 returned 94.5 metres at 0.73 g/t Au and 2.34 g/t Ag, while CV26-017 returned 85.3 metres at 0.52 g/t Au. Three rigs are now active — one RC and two diamond core — on the 30,000m Phase 1 program with roughly 31% complete, targeting an updated mineral resource estimate ahead of a pre-feasibility study planned for 2027. Battle Mountain is Nevada's most productive gold trend, and Roxmore's consistent bulk-tonnage intercepts confirm Converse as a large-system open-pit candidate that plays to the heap-leach economics that defined the trend's historic producers.

headline: LITHIUM MINERS POST BIGGEST H1 PROFITS IN 3 YEARS — Tianqi And Ganfeng Strong As Battery Storage Demand Overwhelms Supply Assumptions
snippet: Bloomberg reported August 31 that lithium producers from China to Australia posted their best first-half profits in three years as the fast-growing energy storage sector — grid-scale batteries for solar and wind integration — absorbed supply that the 2024–2025 lithium bear market had been expected to keep in oversupply. Tianqi Lithium Corp. and Ganfeng Lithium Group each reported their strongest H1 net income since 2023, with Tianqi specifically forecasting a tight market for the rest of 2026 due to accelerating demand and 'disruptive factors' for supply. The H1 2026 data confirms that the lithium price recovery now in its ninth month has genuine margin expansion behind it — not just forward speculation — which typically precedes a sustained re-rating of junior developers in the next tier of the supply chain.

headline: LME COPPER WAREHOUSES DRAIN 42 STRAIGHT SESSIONS — 107,050 Tonnes Left In London As US Tariff Rush Pulls Metal; Copper Holds Near Record $14,830/Tonne
snippet: Open tonnage at London Metal Exchange copper warehouses fell to 107,050 metric tonnes — down from 166,775 MT just a week prior and approaching multi-decade lows — in what is now the longest consecutive LME copper inventory decline since 2014 at 42 straight sessions. The drain reflects US refined copper imports hitting a 12-year monthly high of over 200,000 metric tonnes in July 2026 as traders rush to beat potential January 2027 tariff implementation on refined copper. Meanwhile Comex stocks have swelled to nearly three times LME holdings. The bifurcation between inventory locations is a symptom of genuine market tightness, not just arbitrage: with Codelco, Grasberg, and Kamoa-Kakula all running below capacity, physical supply cannot refill either pool. Copper trades at approximately $6.73/lb ($14,830/tonne), the highest level since August's record close.

headline: SPROTT: URANIUM MINERS UP 21% IN AUGUST AS UTILITY BUYING ACCELERATES — Kazatomprom's 10% Production Cut Deepens Structural Deficit; Spot Near $90/Lb
snippet: Sprott's August uranium market report documents the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index rising 17.01% and junior uranium miners surging 21.75% for the month — outperforming bullion-linked equities and most commodities — as utility companies moved earlier to secure supply and equity/ETF inflows signalled renewed institutional conviction. On the supply side, Kazatomprom intentionally reduced 2026 production guidance by approximately 10% to balance the market, effectively acting as a supply-side constraint that reinforces pricing above $89/lb. The structural uranium deficit — mine production consistently below reactor consumption — is expected to deepen through 2030 as existing reactor refurbishments complete and Small Modular Reactor orders accelerate globally. For junior uranium developers in Athabasca Basin and Kazakhstan-adjacent jurisdictions, a sustained $85–100/lb price environment reopens projects that were uneconomic at $55/lb.

headline: GOLD SWOT: PALLADIUM JOINS PRECIOUS METALS RALLY ON WEAK JOBS DATA — September Rate Hike Odds Starting To Ease; Gold Holds $4,400+ Support
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT report finds the precious metals complex catching a bid from weaker-than-expected US jobs data — a report that has reduced the market's confidence in a consecutive September FOMC rate hike after August 31's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks by Chair Warsh. Palladium notably joined gold and silver in advancing on the data, suggesting broader precious metals appetite rather than isolated gold safe-haven demand. Key strengths in the analysis include central bank buying persistence, physical silver demand from China's solar manufacturing sector, and the gold miners' August re-rating confirming institutional participation rather than just retail speculation. The framing for retail investors: when weak economic data shifts rate expectations even marginally, it tends to relieve the headwind that had been the main bear case for gold since May.

headline: GOLD STOCKS ENTER THEIR STRONGEST SEASON — Autumn Rally Averages 15-25% In Bull Market Years; Miners Still 30-40% Off 2026 Highs
snippet: GoldSeek's seasonal analysis for gold equities finds that the autumn rally — historically running from late June through late September — is among the most consistent seasonal patterns in the junior mining sector, averaging 15-25% gains in established bull market years. With GDX and senior producers still 30-40% below their January 2026 highs despite gold trading above $4,400, the entry point entering September has historically been one of the best risk-reward setups of the calendar year. The analysis notes that September 2026 has an additional catalyst: the post-Warsh hawkishness priced into rate markets may be overstated, and any softening of Fed language into the September FOMC meeting would remove the primary headwind that drove August's post-peak selloff in gold equities.
